description_good_justification: README.md opens with a one-line description: 'C2PA manifest embedding for AI/ML model container formats: GGUF, SafeTensors, and ONNX', plus an Overview section explaining the mechanism and supported formats.
interact_justification: README.md 'Quick Start' shows how to obtain the crate (crates.io/npm/PyPI install commands), CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to contribute (fork/branch/PR), and SECURITY.md/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md list contact points (admin@writerslogic.com, GitHub Security Advisories) for feedback.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' section: fork repo, branch from main, add tests, run cargo test/clippy/fmt, open a PR. Confirms PR-based workflow.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md specifies concrete acceptance requirements: cargo test --all-features must pass, cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings must be clean, cargo fmt --all -- --check must pass, and Conventional Commits style is required.
floss_license_justification: Cargo.toml declares license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"; both LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE are FLOSS licenses.
floss_license_osi_justification: Both MIT and Apache License 2.0 are OSI-approved licenses (https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT, https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0). GitHub's own license detection on the repo also reports Apache-2.0 (spdx_id 'Apache-2.0' via `gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-ml`).
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT exist at repo root (/Volumes/A/c2pa-ml/LICENSE-APACHE, /Volumes/A/c2pa-ml/LICENSE-MIT), the standard location, and README.md's License section links to both.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md documents installation (crates.io/npm/PyPI), Quick Start usage examples for embed/read/verify/detect, and a Design section explaining per-format behavior. docs.rs badge links to generated API docs (Cargo.toml has [package.metadata.docs.rs] all-features = true).
documentation_interface_justification: README.md documents the public API surface (embed_manifest, read_manifest, read_manifest_uri, verify, Format::detect) with input/output types shown in code examples, and Rust doc comments exist in src/*.rs (e.g. src/sha2.rs, src/binding.rs) that render on docs.rs.
sites_https_justification: Repository is hosted at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-ml (HTTPS). Package registries linked in README (crates.io, npmjs.com, pypi.org) are all HTTPS-only.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled and public (`gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-ml` reports has_issues: true) at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-ml/issues, is URL-addressable, searchable, and requires no proprietary client to read or file (GitHub Discussions is not enabled: has_discussions: false, but Issues alone satisfies this criterion).
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and commit messages are in English; issue templates in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ are in English.
maintained_justification: git log shows 16 commits between 2026-07-13 and 2026-08-22 (most recent commit efc8862, 2026-08-22), well within the last 60 days of the current date (2026-08-26); Dependabot PRs are actively opened/merged (issue #6 closed).
repo_public_justification: `gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-ml` reports private: false; repo is at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-ml.
repo_track_justification: Repo uses git; `git log` shows each commit with author, timestamp, and message (e.g. 'efc8862 docs: add title and tagline... David Condrey 2026-08-22').
repo_interim_justification: git log shows commits between the v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 tags (e.g. 5db00fc, 6c77fe4, 99c8ac6, e2547ec, 2baf96d, c84877d, 38dd8b9 all fall between the two tagged releases), not just release-only commits.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository is a git repository (distributed VCS), hosted on GitHub.
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml version field (currently 0.2.0) is unique per release and matches git tags v0.1.0 and v0.2.0; release.yml CI job 'Tag matches crate version' enforces the tag equals the Cargo.toml version before publishing.
version_semver_justification: Versions follow SemVer (0.1.0, 0.2.0 in Cargo.toml and git tags v0.1.0/v0.2.0).
version_tags_justification: `git tag` lists v0.1.0 and v0.2.0; release.yml is triggered `on: push: tags: ['v*.*.*']`.
release_notes_justification: GitHub Releases exist for v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 (`gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-ml/releases`), created via `gh release create --tag --generate-notes` in .github/workflows/release.yml's github-release job, giving each release a structured, human-readable notes page (categorized PR/commit summary plus a compare link), not a raw commit log.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed in any release to date (no security advisories exist for writerslogic/c2pa-ml), so there is nothing yet to identify in release notes.
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled with structured templates: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml, feature_request.yml, and config.yml (blank issues disabled, directs to GitHub Issues). CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting Issues' section documents this process.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is used as the tracker for individual issues; `gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-ml/issues` shows numbered, individually tracked issues/PRs (#1-#7).
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: No external user bug reports have been filed against this repo in the last 2-12 months to establish a response-rate track record; the only tracker activity is automated Dependabot dependency-update PRs (#1-#7 per gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-ml/issues), one of which (#6) was merged, but this does not demonstrate a pattern of responding to user-submitted bug reports specifically.). Marked unknown rather than asserting Unmet on a vacuous condition.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests have been filed (only Dependabot PRs exist in the tracker); marked unknown rather than a vacuous status.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-ml/issues is a public, searchable archive of all reports and responses (open and closed), including closed issue #6.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process: GitHub Security Advisories (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-ml/security/advisories/new) or email admin@writerslogic.com, explicitly asking that public issues not be used for vulnerabilities.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md explains two private channels: GitHub Security Advisories (private by design) and direct email to admin@writerslogic.com.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months (no security advisories or related issues exist for this repo), so there is no response-time data to evaluate.
build_justification: Cargo (cargo build) is the automated build system for the Rust crate; wasm-pack builds the WASM/npm target and maturin builds the Python wheel, both invoked automatically in .github/workflows/release.yml.
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo, the standard/common Rust build tool, plus wasm-pack and maturin, the standard tools for Rust's WASM and PyO3/Python packaging respectively — all conventional for this language ecosystem.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, wasm-pack, and maturin are all FLOSS; no proprietary build tooling is required (confirmed via CONTRIBUTING.md's 'cargo build' / 'cargo test' setup instructions and .github/workflows/*.yml).
test_justification: Automated FLOSS test suite exists: unit tests (#[test]) across src/base64.rs, src/asset_type.rs, src/error.rs, src/gguf.rs, src/onnx.rs, src/format.rs, src/safetensors.rs, src/binding.rs, src/json.rs, src/sha2.rs, plus an integration suite at tests/roundtrip.rs. CONTRIBUTING.md documents running it via `cargo test`.
test_invocation_justification: Tests are run with `cargo test`, the standard invocation for Rust, as documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and used in .github/workflows/ci.yml's 'test' job.
test_most_justification: 89 #[test] functions found across src/*.rs and tests/roundtrip.rs (`grep -rn '#\[test\]' src/*.rs tests/*.rs | wc -l` = 89) covering each format module (gguf, safetensors, onnx), binding/hash logic, and edge cases (NIST SHA-256 test vectors in src/sha2.rs), indicating broad functional coverage relative to the crate's small surface area.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo test` on every push to main and every pull request (job 'test'), plus a separate MSRV check job.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' step 2 explicitly states 'Make changes, add tests, run cargo test --all-features', establishing a policy that changes come with tests.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature commits pair implementation with tests in the same commit, e.g. 6c77fe4 'feat: conform ONNX and SafeTensors embedding to the specification' and 5db00fc 'feat: uniform Error::code, verified MSRV, and integration tests' (which added tests/roundtrip.rs) show tests landing alongside functional changes.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the add-tests-with-changes policy directly in the 'Submitting Changes' section (step 2: 'Make changes, add tests...').
warnings_justification: clippy (Rust's standard FLOSS linter) is enabled and enforced with `-D warnings` in .github/workflows/ci.yml ('cargo clippy --features python -- -D warnings' and a wasm32-target clippy pass), and rustfmt formatting is checked (`cargo fmt --all -- --check`).
warnings_fixed_justification: CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) fails the build on any clippy warning via `-D warnings`, so warnings must be fixed before merge; CONTRIBUTING.md instructs contributors to run the same clippy/fmt checks locally before submitting.
warnings_strict_justification: Clippy is run with `-D warnings` (deny, the strictest common setting) across two targets (default + wasm32) and two feature sets (python feature, default), plus a separate MSRV `cargo check` job in ci.yml — a strict, multi-target configuration.
know_secure_design_justification: src/lib.rs:52 `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` rules out memory-unsafe code by construction. SECURITY.md's Supply-chain security section documents mitigations for common attack classes: GitHub Actions pinned to full commit SHAs (against tag-mutation attacks), OpenSSF Scorecard, Dependency Review, and Dependabot running in CI, and build provenance on releases where the registry supports it.
know_common_errors_justification: SECURITY.md's Supply-chain security section documents specific mitigations for common attack classes: GitHub Actions pinned to full commit SHAs (against tag-mutation attacks), OpenSSF Scorecard, Dependency Review, and Dependabot running in CI to catch known-vulnerable dependencies, and build provenance on releases.
crypto_published_justification: src/sha2.rs implements only the publicly published/reviewed SHA-256/384/512 algorithms (NIST FIPS 180-4), used in src/binding.rs for C2PA hard-binding hash computation; no proprietary or unreviewed algorithms are used.
crypto_call_justification: The crate reimplements SHA-256/384/512 from scratch in src/sha2.rs rather than calling a dedicated, widely-reviewed crypto crate (e.g. RustCrypto's `sha2`). The file's own doc comment explains the tradeoff: 'hash is the one primitive where writing it yourself is uncontroversial... What is given up is speed' — a deliberate reimplementation to keep the crate dependency-free, which is the opposite of this criterion's recommendation.
crypto_floss_justification: All hashing (src/sha2.rs) is implemented in Rust and is itself FLOSS (MIT OR Apache-2.0), fully implementable with FLOSS tools.
crypto_keylength_justification: This crate performs no key-based cryptography (no signing/encryption keys); it only computes content hashes for C2PA hard binding. Manifest signing is explicitly out of scope (README.md 'Scope' section: 'Manifest construction, signing, and content (hard/soft) binding are out of scope; use the official C2PA SDK').
crypto_working_justification: src/sha2.rs implements only SHA-256/384/512; no broken algorithm (MD4, MD5, single-DES, RC4, Dual_EC_DRBG) or broken cipher mode is used anywhere in src/.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Only SHA-256/384/512 are used (src/sha2.rs, src/binding.rs Algorithm enum); SHA-1 and CBC-in-SSH do not appear anywhere in the codebase.
crypto_pfs_justification: This crate performs no key agreement or network handshakes; it is a local file-format library with no networking/session-key code.
crypto_password_storage_justification: This crate has no authentication or password-storage functionality; it is a manifest-embedding library for model file formats.
crypto_random_justification: This crate generates no cryptographic keys or nonces; it only computes deterministic content hashes (SHA-2) over caller-supplied bytes.
delivery_mitm_justification: Packages are delivered via crates.io, npmjs.com, and PyPI, all served exclusively over HTTPS; .github/workflows/release.yml publishes to these registries over their standard HTTPS APIs (cargo publish, npm publish, pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash-only integrity check over plain HTTP is used anywhere; all package delivery is via HTTPS registries (crates.io, npm, PyPI) which perform their own transport and package-integrity verification.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No open, publicly known medium+ severity vulnerabilities exist for this repo (no security advisories listed on https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-ml/security/advisories); the one dependency security fix seen (c84877d 'fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29') was applied promptly.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities have been reported against this project to date; Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) is configured for weekly dependency scanning to catch and surface future ones quickly.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Searched tracked source/config/doc files (*.rs, *.toml, *.md) for private-key markers and hardcoded API-key/secret patterns; none found. Publishing credentials (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN) are referenced only as GitHub Actions `secrets.*` in .github/workflows/release.yml, never as literal values in the repo.
static_analysis_justification: clippy, a FLOSS static-analysis tool for Rust, is run in .github/workflows/ci.yml ('check' job) on every push/PR to main and again in release.yml's 'verify' job before every release, across two targets (native + wasm32) and the python feature set.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Only clippy (a correctness/style linter) is run; there is no evidence of a vulnerability-focused static analyzer (e.g. cargo-audit, cargo-deny, CodeQL, or Semgrep) in .github/workflows/ — searched with `grep -rli 'codeql|semgrep|cargo-audit|cargo-deny|scorecard' .github` with no matches, despite SECURITY.md claiming 'OpenSSF Scorecard... run in CI' (no such workflow file exists in .github/workflows/).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CI enforces `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, so any static-analysis finding blocks merge until fixed (.github/workflows/ci.yml 'check' job and release.yml 'verify' job).
static_analysis_often_justification: clippy runs on every push to main and every pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml, triggers: push to main, pull_request to main), i.e. on every commit reaching those refs.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (e.g. fuzzing via cargo-fuzz, or a sanitizer run) was found in .github/workflows/ or elsewhere in the repo; only static clippy checks and cargo test are run.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: No `unsafe` memory-unsafe code was found in a manual review of src/*.rs during this audit (the crate is safe-Rust parsing/rewriting of binary formats); this is standard-Rust code without C/C++ memory-unsafety concerns, so no memory-safety dynamic tool is required.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic-analysis configuration exists in this repo (see dynamic_analysis above), so there is no assertion-enabling config to evaluate.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic-analysis tool is currently run against this project (see dynamic_analysis above), so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to have fixed.
